name: Loop boundary: iterates exactly over valid column indices vs. runs one index past the end (<=)
side_a: No deduct if the traversal stays within the array bounds — i.e. the for-loop condition uses a strict `<` against the row length (or uses an enhanced for-loop over the row), so every access `board[targetRow][col]` is legal.
side_b: Deduct if the traversal exceeds the array bounds — e.g. the loop condition is `col <= board[targetRow].length`, causing an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on the final iteration and preventing the sum/color check from ever completing.

name: colors compared with equals() (possibly negated) vs. compared with == / != reference operators
side_a: Do not deduct when the two color values are compared using the equals() method, including the negated form `!a.equals(b)` inside an if-condition; the use of equals() is the behavior the sub-item actually scores.
side_b: Deduct whenever the colors are compared with the reference operators `==` or `!=` (e.g., `currentSpace.getColor() != firstColor`), even if everything else — storing the first color in a variable, calling getColor() on real Space objects, using the boolean result correctly — is perfect.

name: Off-by-one / out-of-bounds loop bound in the summation loop: tolerated as an 'incorrect sum' vs treated as failing to sum the row's points
side_a: Do not deduct when the response initializes a points variable and accumulates `space.getPoints()` inside a loop over the row, even if the loop bound is wrong and would throw at runtime (e.g., `col <= board[targetRow].length`). The bound error affects correctness of the sum, not whether the points variable was initialized or the point method was called.
side_b: Deduct when the loop's bounds are wrong such that the traversal does not validly cover the row's spaces (e.g., `col <= board[targetRow].length` runs past the last index and throws), on the grounds that no valid sum of the row's point values is ever produced.
